added_queue_rows.source_line: | 1751 | 3200 / OPG-388 | List colorings of edge-critical graphs | 0.0585 | 5.0 | 1 | unknown | unsolved | ≥5; total unknown |  | One newly accepted substantive partial round in this continuation, with two parallel directions counted together; an earlier screen exists and total lifetime turns are unknown. Complete proofs: at most four arbitrary exceptional lists, star/triangle support, matching plus one, strict residual deficit, full degree-two case, and up to Δ+1 genuinely changed one-color substitutions. Nonconstant-preserving finite-palette reductions; subdivided-K4 arbitrary-list case follows known Kaul–Mudrock Lemma 3. Independently audited census through seven nonisolated vertices and four-palette scans of six graphs; larger graphs remain tested only in the four-palette domain. General conjecture unresolved; no novelty claim. Authored proofs and audits: unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3200_critical_list_partials_20261012/README.md. Second accepted substantive round: for Δ=3, arbitrary exceptional three-element lists on a five-cycle are colorable, and five one-color substitutions on arbitrary support are colorable when omitted base colors vary. The independently audited strict-residual-certificate classification covers 20 five-edge subcubic line-graph types and 72,700,180 support/family decisions, with 65 normalized failures in 34 orbits; 14 of 16 profile-11222 classes have a universal incident-pair Hall escape. These are method failures, not bad-list counterexamples. Complete proofs, explicit criticality examples and one same-exterior-set Kempe repair are retained; omitted raw machine collections cannot be reconstructed from the prose alone. The all-five-arbitrary-support assertion and general conjecture remain unresolved by this round; no novelty claim. Authored second-round proofs and audits: unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3200_five_exception_partials_20261012/README.md. Two accepted rounds in this continuation; total lifetime attempts remain unknown. Accepted third substantive partial round: every nonconstant exact-Δ-list assignment on a finite simple graph of actual maximum degree Δ that is not Δ-edge-colorable but becomes so after every edge deletion is colorable whenever at most five lists differ from some Δ-element palette. Complete symbolic exactly-five proofs cover Δ=3 and Δ≥4, with first-round one-through-four and arbitrary-star inputs, the complete Δ=2 odd-cycle case and vacuous Δ≤1. Any hypothetical bad nonconstant assignment must differ from every Δ-palette on at least six edges. This closes the preceding arbitrary-support five-list frontier, without resolving the general conjecture or establishing novelty. The earlier large classification is not a proof dependency; computations are corroborative, and raw machine records are excluded. Complete third-round proofs, audits and exact dependencies: unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3200_five_list_theorem_20261012/README.md. Three accepted substantive rounds are confirmed in this continuation; total lifetime attempts remain unknown. Accepted a fourth substantive partial round: every nonconstant exact-three-list assignment on a finite simple subcubic graph that is not three-edge-colorable but becomes so after every edge deletion is colorable if two colors occur in every list. The complete symbolic proof has no exception-count bound and uses palette collapse, a mixed-vertex minority edge, matching recoloring and restoration; no preceding five-exception theorem or finite enumeration is a premise. Within this common-two-color family, uncolorability is equivalent to constancy. The complete six-edge local-method frontier is K4/K2,3; K4 is excluded by ambient criticality. A fully explicit thirteen-edge critical K2,3 example preserves all deletion-matching certificates, a fixed-choice method failure and a successful reversed-palette coloring. A complementary bounded six-unit method classification covers 1,154,461 normalized cases with pointwise three-program agreement and leaves 12 method records, of which four K4 records cannot occur critically. Eight actual examples remain fully list-colorable with the selected edge exterior; six nonetheless defeat every ordinary-deletion-derived repair for that edge. The complete explicit seven-edge nonextension example retracts the false implication from repair failure to selected-edge-exterior impossibility. This does not settle arbitrary nonconstant lists or establish novelty. Full proofs, substantive independent audits and precise reproduction boundaries: unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3200_common_core_partials_20261012/README.md. Four accepted substantive rounds in this continuation; total lifetime attempts unknown. Accepted the fifth and final substantive round in this continuation: on a finite simple graph of maximum degree at most three that is not three-edge-colorable but becomes so after every edge deletion, exact-three edge lists with nonempty total intersection are list-edge-colorable if and only if nonconstant. The complete symbolic proof has no graph-order, palette or exception-count bound and is independently accepted without correction. A permissible color class of a deletion coloring leaves exactly one odd cycle; two local critical cycles detect nonconstant reduced lists. This is not a claim about arbitrary degree-three-covering matchings. Full proof and substantive independent audit: unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3200_common_one_color_20261012/README.md. The general conjecture stays unsolved; subcubic empty-intersection cases remain except those covered by prior results. The third edition already covers every degree with at most five exceptions. Five confirmed substantive continuation rounds; lifetime total unknown. No sixth research round. The same fifth round also establishes the exact fixed-matching criterion: every odd residual cycle must have nonconstant reduced two-lists, and the complete critical-cycle family is connected by edge intersection. An explicit 25-vertex, 37-edge critical graph has a cubic-vertex-covering matching leaving C3+C3+C19; this disproves uniqueness for arbitrary covering matchings, not list colorability. A seven-edge example separates a failed matching choice from a successful full coloring. Complete matching proof, constructions and substantive independent audit: unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3200_common_one_color_20261012/METHODS.md and AUDIT_METHODS.md. The prior all-degree five-exception theorem is at unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3200_five_list_theorem_20261012/THEOREM.md. |  |
